RTT/TTY engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume RTT or TTY capability in the binary covers storefront language. iOS, carriers, and Connect actually separate real-time text on phone calls from product-page copy:

  • RTT relay & carrier routing — system and carrier integration that routes Real-Time Text during PSTN phone calls. Controls whether buyers can type and read text on an active call. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • TTY mode & hardware TTY pairing — software TTY keyboards, hardware TTY device connection, and TTY relay settings under Settings → Accessibility → RTT/TTY. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains RTT/TTY call accessibility value to buyers.
  • In-call text relay UI — engineering work for Send as Text panels, RTT conversation threads, and TTY character entry during calls. Listing copy should match what your gallery shows — an RTT call panel is not a Live Caption subtitle bar unless that is what the screenshot depicts.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of RTT/TTY support in the app.

Working RTT/TTY call flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. RTT-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

RTT and TTY call accessibility marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe RTT/TTY workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

RTT vs Live Caption vs Live Speech

US pages use "RTT", "Real-Time Text", or "TTY." China storefront copy often uses 实时文本 for Real-Time Text on phone calls, keeps RTT and TTY as recognized acronyms when buyers search for them, or uses 电话实时文本 and 听障通话辅助 when your English listing already frames hearing/speech call accessibility that way — depending on whether you mean system RTT during carrier calls, in-app TTY companions, or call text-relay demos. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope and avoids conflating RTT with 实时字幕 (Live Caption media subtitles) or 实时语音 / 键入朗读 (Live Speech type-to-speak) when your screenshots show RTT call panels, not caption bars or speak-aloud keyboards.

Software TTY vs hardware TTY

Screenshot galleries may label software TTY keyboards separately from hardware TTY device pairing. Buyers searching for call accessibility apps distinguish on-screen TTY entry from external TTY hardware — match what your English listing and screenshots actually show.

RTT on phone calls vs Live Voicemail transcription

RTT sends typed text during an active phone call. Live Voicemail transcribes a message while the caller leaves voicemail — different buyer intent and screenshot vocabulary. Do not reuse Live Voicemail framing on RTT call thread frames unless that is what the screenshot depicts.

RTT vs Call Recording

Call Recording saves audio from answered calls. RTT relays typed characters in real time for accessibility — opposite marketing story from recording badges unless your English gallery explicitly shows both on separate frames.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need RTT/TTY search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 实时文本, RTT, TTY, and 电话实时文本 each signal different intent from Live Caption, Live Speech, or Hearing Devices keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "RTT" or "Real-Time Text" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

Promotional text refreshes

RTT/TTY feature launches and carrier RTT availability updates often land in the 170-character promotional text field above the description — updatable without a new binary. See Promotional text in Simplified Chinese when your RTT/TTY pitch lives in promo text rather than the long description.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement RTT, TTY, or CallKit telephony APIs?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. RTT/TTY OS integration, CallKit RTT routing, TTY hardware pairing, and in-call text relay UI engineering are outside scope.

How is RTT listing copy different from Live Caption or Live Speech?

RTT listing copy covers Real-Time Text and TTY during carrier phone calls — typed text relay for hearing and speech accessibility. Live Caption covers on-device captions for media and heard audio. Live Speech covers type-to-speak aloud in conversations. Those are different buyer stories with different screenshot vocabulary.

How is this different from Live Voicemail, Call Recording, or Silence Unknown Callers?

Live Voicemail covers voicemail transcription while a caller leaves a message. Call Recording covers recording answered calls. Silence Unknown Callers covers silencing unknown numbers. Hold Assist covers wait-on-hold automation. RTT covers typed text during an active phone call — a different framing on the product page.

How is RTT different from Hearing Devices, Voice Control, or Dwell Control?

Hearing Devices covers hearing-aid pairing and audio routing. Voice Control covers spoken UI commands. Dwell Control covers pointer-rest dwell-to-click timing. RTT covers real-time text on phone calls — different accessibility surface and keywords.

Does localizing my listing change RTT or TTY behavior on phone calls?

No. RTT relay routing, TTY mode toggles, and call text delivery come from iOS, your carrier, and your binary — not Connect listing fields. AppLocale covers product-page marketing copy only.
